entities.summary: Luis de Ávila y Zúñiga was a Spanish historian who played a crucial role in the development of the annals of the world, a comprehensive historical record of human civilization from prehistory to the digital age. He was born in the 16th century in the region of Andalusia, Spain, and spent his life studying and recording the events of the past. His work focused on the medieval period, and he is particularly known for his detailed accounts of the history of the Spanish kingdoms. Luis de Ávila y Zúñiga's contributions to the annals of the world have had a lasting impact on our understanding of the medieval period, and his work continues to be studied by historians and scholars today. He died on October 4, 1573, in the city of Seville, leaving behind a legacy of historical scholarship that has endured for centuries. The annals of the world, which he helped to establish, remain an essential resource for anyone seeking to understand the complexities of human history.
